summary: HOLD for two reasons. (1) The key range is wrong: seq = seq_lens[b]-7+j treats seq_lens as the post-block length, but seq_lens is the prefix length (positions = seq_lens+j, cache_seqlens = seq_lens+8). Each pseudo-query would attend a window shifted 8 keys into the past, missing its own and the preceding block keys: an every-key/causal rule break. (2) It duplicates the B=1 band of sliding-verify-sk-pseudo-decode-s1 on the same row. Unhold, with the fix below, only if that run's B=1 band falls back to FA3 or lands above ~12.5 us shape.
justification: Mechanism (once fixed): 8 pseudo-requests x 2 kv heads x 16 splits = 256 programs. Each does about the same work per program as master's decode (~128 keys), so the kernel should sit between decode_1 (10.4 us, 32 programs) and decode_16 (12.9 us, 512 programs), call it ~11 us. Add pre-attn ~1.3 us and one launch gap, ~13-13.5 us, against the 16.7 us shape. That is a plausible ~20% on sliding verify_1 (weight 46, 62% of the verify_1 load). WEAKEST LINK: the arithmetic error above, plus the fact that the 16 tests never exercise this route (no sliding q_len 8 test at batch 1). The first correctness check would be the judge's timed-call check, after a full run is spent.
confounders: sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate / sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv (landed): this edits _sliding_fused_kernel, which serves every sliding decode row. PSEUDO=0 must be the master specialization (constexpr-gated, so the Triton cache key differs and the decode code is unchanged). Expect no decode movement.

fused-preattention-triton (landed): it writes the 8 new K/V rows before this kernel. Correctness now depends on that store (the S-1 new-key branch is skipped), so its cache rows are the attended keys. That matches what the judge checks ('reference attending to your own new entries').

sliding-verify-sk-pseudo-decode-s1 (queued, p1): same row, same idea (verify token = decode query), different kernel. Running both now buys a second implementation of one row with no new information unless the CUDA one loses at B=1.
interference: No companion while held. If unheld, it is attributable on its own: only sliding verify_1 changes, against an FA3 base row, and every other row is master code.
rules_flags: WRONG KEY RANGE (blocking): reference query j of request b is at p = seq_lens[b]+j and attends keys [max(0,p-W+1), p] (reference.py lines ~322-330). The hypothesis sets seq = seq_lens[b]-7+j with 'key t valid iff seq-window <= t < seq', i.e. keys [seq_lens+j-7-W, seq_lens+j-8]. That window is shifted down by 8 and drops keys p-7..p, including the query's own key. Fix: P = positions[b*8+j] = seq_lens[b]+j, attended range [max(0, P-(W-1)), P] inclusive (exactly W keys), all read from cache. Equivalently, exclusive end = cache_seqlens[b]-7+j.

Master's decode code splits the OLD keys [max(0,seq-(W-1)), seq) and attends the new key at seq from registers in program S-1. If PSEUDO skips the S-1 new-key branch, the split coverage must extend to include key P itself, or each row loses one key. State the chunk range as [lo, P+1) under PSEUDO.
Per-token RoPE: q must use positions[b*8+j] (the change says so). The cache keys were roped by pre-attention at their own positions. OK.
Query precision bf16 is finer than E4M3 (allowed). KV FP8 unchanged.
Counters: use a distinct _counters key so a graph that also captures decode batch 8 cannot share ticket memory (as stated).
open_questions: UNHOLD CONDITION: sliding-verify-sk-pseudo-decode-s1 prints B=1 band FA3 (fallback/timing) or its routed sliding verify_1 shape is > ~12.5 us. Then run this with the corrected range and an import-time fp32 windowed-causal self-check at B=1 (lens 5, 2000, 2050, 80000; kv_scale 1 and 0.25), failure keeping FA3.

If unheld, consider S=8 vs 16 splits per pseudo-request as a prepare-timed choice (256 vs 128 programs). Decode evidence (sliding-decode32-splits-8) says fewer splits can win when programs exceed ~256.
